Anatomy-01.question: ১) Post translational modification does not occur in-
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is Mitochondria. 

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Mitochondria – Some mitochondrial proteins undergo post-translational processing, including cleavage and modification.

  • RER – Major site of early protein modifications such as folding, disulfide bond formation, and N-linked glycosylation.

  • Golgi complex – Performs further modifications such as glycosylation, sulfation, and phosphorylation.

High-yield points:

Protein processing pathway:

DNA → mRNA → Ribosome (translation) → RER → Golgi → Functional protein

Examples of post-translational modifications:

  • Glycosylation

  • Phosphorylation

  • Acetylation

  • Proteolytic cleavage

  • Disulfide bond formation

Exam pearl:
Ribosome = translation site, not post-translational modification site.

Anatomy-01.question: ২) Functions of Golgi apparatus excludes-
Anatomy-01.option4: Necessary for the synthesis of acrosome in spermatozoa
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is autophagy. Autophagy is a cellular degradation process involving lysosomes, where damaged organelles and cytoplasmic components are broken down. It is not a direct function of the Golgi apparatus.

The other options are functions of the Golgi apparatus:

  • Modification of new proteins – Golgi modifies proteins through processes such as glycosylation, sulfation, and phosphorylation.

  • Packaging enzymes for lysosomes – Golgi packages lysosomal enzymes by adding mannose-6-phosphate (M6P) tags.

  • Necessary for synthesis of acrosome in spermatozoa – The acrosome develops from the Golgi apparatus during spermatogenesis.

High-yield points:

Functions of Golgi apparatus:

  • Modification of proteins and lipids

  • Packaging and sorting of proteins

  • Formation of secretory vesicles

  • Formation of lysosomes

  • Formation of sperm acrosome

Autophagy:

  • Lysosome-mediated degradation of intracellular components

  • Important in cell survival and removal of damaged organelles

Exam pearl:
Golgi → Modify, package, sort, form lysosomes & acrosome
Lysosome → Digest and recycle (autophagy)

Anatomy-01.question: ৩) Regarding cells of mononuclear phagocytic system, which of these are true?
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is Liver–Kupffer cells. The mononuclear phagocytic system (MPS) consists of cells derived from monocytes/macrophages that perform phagocytosis and antigen presentation. Kupffer cells are the resident macrophages of the liver and are a classic component of the MPS.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Skin–Langerhans cells – These are dendritic antigen-presenting cells of the skin. They are immune cells but are not considered part of the mononuclear phagocytic system in classic descriptions.

  • Bone–osteoblast – Osteoblasts are bone-forming cells, not phagocytic cells. (Osteoclasts are derived from the monocyte-macrophage lineage.)

  • Brain–astrocyte – Astrocytes are neuroglial support cells. (Microglia, not astrocytes, are the macrophage cells of the CNS.)

High-yield points:

Mononuclear phagocytic system examples:

  • Blood → Monocytes

  • Liver → Kupffer cells

  • Brain → Microglia

  • Connective tissue → Histiocytes

  • Lung → Alveolar macrophages

  • Bone → Osteoclasts

Exam pearl:
Macrophage of liver = Kupffer cell
Macrophage of brain = Microglia
Macrophage of bone = Osteoclast

Anatomy-01.question: ৪) Growing end is present in-
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is lower end of tibia. The growing end (epiphysis) of a long bone is the end where the epiphyseal plate contributes more actively to longitudinal growth. In the tibia, the lower end is the growing end.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Lower end of humerus – Not the growing end. The upper end of humerus contributes more to growth.

  • Lower end of radius – The upper end of radius is the growing end.

  • Upper end of ulna – The lower end of ulna is the growing end.

High-yield points:

Growing ends of common long bones:

  • Humerus → Upper end

  • Radius → Upper end

  • Ulna → Lower end

  • Tibia → Lower end

  • Femur → Lower end

Mnemonic:
“ELFU” rule (towards the elbow):

  • End near elbow grows less

  • Femur and Tibia grow more at knee (femur lower, tibia upper/lower distinction varies by exam context)

Classic exam fact:
Lower end of tibia = growing end.

Anatomy-01.question: ৫) Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium is not found in the lining of-
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is larynx. Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium (respiratory epithelium) lines most of the conducting respiratory tract, but it is not found throughout the larynx. Most of the larynx is lined by stratified squamous epithelium because of mechanical stress from passage of food and voice production.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Trachea – Lined by typical pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium with goblet cells.

  • Auditory tube (Eustachian tube) – Lined by respiratory epithelium (pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium).

  • Lacrimal sac – Lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium.

High-yield points:

Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium sites:

  • Trachea

  • Bronchi

  • Nasal cavity

  • Auditory tube

  • Lacrimal sac

Exceptions in respiratory tract:

  • Vocal cords → stratified squamous epithelium

  • Oropharynx/laryngopharynx → stratified squamous epithelium

Exam pearl:
Respiratory epithelium = ciliated pseudostratified columnar + goblet cells.

Anatomy-01.question: ৬) Regarding red muscle fibers
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is blood supply rich. Red muscle fibres (slow-twitch type I fibres) have a rich blood supply due to a high number of capillaries, which provides oxygen for prolonged aerobic activity.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Present in small amount – Red fibres are present in significant amounts, especially in postural muscles.

  • Less mitochondria present – Incorrect. Red muscle fibres contain many mitochondria to support oxidative metabolism.

  • Myofibrils more – Red fibres have fewer and smaller myofibrils compared with white fibres, resulting in less forceful contraction.

High-yield points:

Red muscle fibres (Type I / slow oxidative):

  • Rich blood supply

  • High myoglobin content (red colour)

  • Many mitochondria

  • Slow contraction

  • Resistant to fatigue

  • Used for posture and endurance activities

White muscle fibres (Type II / fast glycolytic):

  • Fewer mitochondria

  • Less blood supply

  • Rapid, powerful contraction

  • Fatigue quickly

Exam pearl:
Red muscle = oxygen-rich + mitochondria-rich + fatigue-resistant.

Anatomy-01.question: ৭) Fibrocartilage found in
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is intervertebral disc. Fibrocartilage is a tough cartilage type containing abundant type I collagen fibres, providing strength and resistance to compression. It is found in the annulus fibrosus of intervertebral discs.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Articular cartilage – Made of hyaline cartilage, covering the surfaces of synovial joints.

  • Larynx – Mainly contains elastic cartilage (epiglottis, arytenoid) and hyaline cartilage (thyroid, cricoid).

  • Bronchi – Contain hyaline cartilage in their walls.

High-yield points:

Types of cartilage and examples:

Hyaline cartilage:

  • Articular cartilage

  • Trachea and bronchi

  • Costal cartilage

  • Nose

Elastic cartilage:

  • Pinna of ear

  • Epiglottis

  • Auditory tube

Fibrocartilage:

  • Intervertebral disc

  • Pubic symphysis

  • Menisci of knee

Exam pearl:
Fibrocartilage = strongest cartilage → intervertebral disc.

Anatomy-01.question: ৮) Ventral component of otic vesicle gives rise to
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is saccule. During development, the otic vesicle (otocyst) differentiates into:

  • Dorsal component → Utricle, semicircular ducts, endolymphatic duct and sac

  • Ventral component → Saccule and cochlear duct

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Utricle – Develops from the dorsal part of the otic vesicle.

  • Semicircular canals – Develop from the dorsal component.

  • Endolymphatic duct – Develops from the dorsal component.

High-yield points:

Otic vesicle derivatives:

Dorsal part:

  • Utricle

  • Semicircular ducts

  • Endolymphatic duct

Ventral part:

  • Saccule

  • Cochlear duct

Mnemonic:
“Dorsal = Dynamic balance, Ventral = Voice (cochlea)”

Anatomy-01.question: ৯) Feature of liquor amnii excludes
Anatomy-01.option2: The fluid gradually increases up to 6th month of pregnancy
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is it restricts fetal movement. Liquor amnii (amniotic fluid) allows free movement of the fetus and prevents restriction of fetal movements. Therefore, restricting fetal movement is not a feature.

The other options are correct because:

  • Watery – Amniotic fluid is a clear, watery fluid.

  • The fluid gradually increases up to 6th month of pregnancy – Amniotic fluid volume increases progressively during pregnancy and reaches a maximum around 32–34 weeks (not exactly the 6th month).

  • It acts as a protective cushion – Amniotic fluid protects the fetus from mechanical injury and maintains a stable environment.

High-yield points:

Functions of liquor amnii:

  • Provides a protective cushion

  • Allows fetal movement and musculoskeletal development

  • Prevents adhesion of fetus to amnion

  • Maintains temperature

  • Helps lung development

Exam pearl:
Amniotic fluid facilitates fetal movement, it does not restrict it.

Anatomy-01.question: ১০) When spermatogenesis begins?
১১) During fusion with sperm cell membrane the stage of oocyte is
১২) Crosses placenta
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is IgG. IgG is the only immunoglobulin that crosses the placenta and provides passive immunity to the fetus and newborn. This occurs through the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) on placental cells.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • IgA – Mainly found in mucosal secretions such as breast milk, saliva, and intestinal secretions; does not cross the placenta.

  • IgM – The largest immunoglobulin; does not cross the placenta. Presence of IgM in fetal blood suggests intrauterine infection.

  • IgD – Mainly functions as a B-cell receptor and does not cross the placenta.

High-yield points:

Immunoglobulin facts:

  • IgG → Crosses placenta; most abundant serum antibody

  • IgA → Mucosal immunity; breast milk

  • IgM → First antibody produced; cannot cross placenta

  • IgE → Allergy and parasites

  • IgD → B-cell receptor

Exam pearl:
Placental antibody transfer = IgG.

Anatomy-01.question: ১৩) Commonest site of ectopic pregnancy
১৪) Normal site of fertilization
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is ampulla of the uterine tube. Normal fertilization usually occurs in the ampullary region of the fallopian tube, where the ovum and sperm meet.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Abdominal cavity – Fertilization does not normally occur here; abdominal pregnancy is a rare ectopic event.

  • Uterine cavity – The uterus is the site of implantation, not fertilization.

  • Isthmus – A narrower part of the uterine tube and is less commonly the site of fertilization.

High-yield points:

Fertilization:

  • Site → Ampulla of fallopian tube

  • Sperm meets ovum → ampulla

  • Zygote then travels to uterus for implantation

Ectopic pregnancy:

  • Most common site → Ampulla of fallopian tube

Exam pearl:
Ampulla = fertilization site + commonest ectopic pregnancy site.

Anatomy-01.question: ১৫) Days required for spermatogenesis
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is 74 days. Spermatogenesis takes approximately 74 days for spermatogonia to develop into mature spermatozoa within the seminiferous tubules. After this, sperm require additional time for maturation and transport through the epididymis.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • 60 days – Shorter than the accepted duration of spermatogenesis.

  • 70 days – Close but not the standard exam value.

  • 84 days – Longer than the usual duration.

High-yield points:

Spermatogenesis:

  • Begins → Puberty

  • Site → Seminiferous tubules

  • Duration → ~74 days

  • Requires → FSH + testosterone

Sequence:
Spermatogonia → Primary spermatocytes → Secondary spermatocytes → Spermatids → Spermatozoa

Exam pearl:
Spermatogenesis = 74 days.

Anatomy-01.question: ১৬) Dorsal root ganglia are derived from
১৭) Lens is derived from
১৮) Retina is derived from
১৯) Skeletal muscle is derived from
২০) Fibrous pericardium develops from
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is paraxial mesoderm. Skeletal muscle develops mainly from paraxial mesoderm, which forms somites. The myotome portion of somites gives rise to skeletal muscles of the trunk and limbs.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Intermediate mesoderm – Forms the urogenital system (kidneys, gonads, genital ducts).

  • Lateral plate mesoderm – Forms connective tissues, cardiovascular system, body wall structures, and smooth muscle of some organs.

  • Chorda-mesoderm (notochordal mesoderm) – Forms the notochord, which later contributes to the nucleus pulposus of intervertebral discs.

High-yield points:

Mesoderm derivatives:

  • Paraxial mesoderm → Somites →

    • Sclerotome → vertebrae and ribs

    • Myotome → skeletal muscle

    • Dermatome → dermis

  • Intermediate mesoderm → Urogenital system

  • Lateral plate mesoderm → Heart, blood vessels, connective tissue

Exam pearl:
Skeletal muscle = Myotome = Paraxial mesoderm.

Anatomy-01.question: ২১) Notochord is derived from
২২) Foregut is supplied by
২৩) Nerve for 2nd pharyngeal arch
২৪) Derivative of 2nd pharyngeal pouch
২৫) Smooth part of right ventricle is derived from
২৬) Which layer of uterus are considered for implant of blastocyst?
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is endometrium. The blastocyst implants into the endometrial lining of the uterus, specifically the functional layer (stratum functionale) of the endometrium.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Perimetrium – The outer serosal layer of the uterus; not involved in implantation.

  • Myometrium – The muscular layer of the uterus responsible for uterine contractions; not the site of normal implantation.

  • Epimetrium – Not a recognized layer of the uterus.

High-yield points:

Layers of uterus:

  1. Endometrium → implantation site

  2. Myometrium → smooth muscle layer

  3. Perimetrium → outer serosal covering

Endometrial changes:

  • Ovulation → secretory phase prepares for implantation

  • Implantation → trophoblast invades endometrium

  • Placenta develops from trophoblast + maternal endometrium

Exam pearl:
Blastocyst implantation = Endometrium (stratum functionale).

Anatomy-01.question: ২৭) Central tendon of diaphragm is developed from
২৮) What is the normal site of implantation?
Anatomy-01.option2: Anterior or posterior wall of the body of the uterus
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is anterior or posterior wall of the body of the uterus. The normal site of implantation is usually the upper part of the uterine cavity, most commonly on the posterior wall of the body of the uterus (often extending to the anterior wall).

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Fundus of uterus – Although implantation may occur near the fundus, it is not considered the most common textbook site.

  • Internal os of the uterus – Implantation near the internal os leads to placenta previa.

  • Cornua of the uterus – Implantation here is abnormal and may result in cornual/interstitial ectopic pregnancy.

High-yield points:

Normal implantation site:

  • Upper posterior wall of uterine body (most common)

  • Sometimes upper anterior wall

Abnormal implantation sites:

  • Lower uterine segment → placenta previa

  • Fallopian tube → ectopic pregnancy

Exam pearl:
Normal implantation = posterior wall of upper body of uterus.

Anatomy-01.question: ২৯) Definitive kidney develops from
৩০) Regarding cell distribution of intermediate filaments, which one is not true?
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is Nestin–neuron. Nestin is an intermediate filament protein mainly expressed in neural stem cells and developing nervous system cells, not mature neurons. Mature neurons contain neurofilaments as their major intermediate filaments.

The other options are correct because:

  • Desmin–muscle cells – Desmin is an intermediate filament found in skeletal, cardiac, and smooth muscle cells.

  • Keratin–epithelial cells – Keratins are intermediate filaments characteristic of epithelial cells.

  • Lamins–nuclei of all cells – Nuclear lamins form the nuclear lamina and are present in the nuclei of most cells.

High-yield points:

Intermediate filaments and distribution:

Intermediate filament Location
Keratin Epithelial cells
Desmin Muscle cells
Vimentin Mesenchymal cells
Neurofilament Neurons
Lamins Nuclear envelope
Nestin Neural stem cells

Exam pearl:
Mature neuron → Neurofilament
Neural stem cell → Nestin.

Anatomy-01.question: ৩১) The sister chromatids of each chromosome separate and migrate towards the opposite pole during-
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is anaphase. During anaphase of mitosis, the centromeres divide and the sister chromatids separate and migrate towards opposite poles of the cell.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Prophase – Chromosomes condense and become visible; spindle formation begins.

  • Metaphase – Chromosomes align at the equatorial plate of the cell.

  • Telophase – Chromosomes reach the poles and nuclear membranes reform.

High-yield points:

Stages of mitosis:

  • Prophase → Chromosome condensation, spindle formation

  • Metaphase → Chromosomes align at equator

  • Anaphase → Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles

  • Telophase → Nuclear envelope reforms

Exam pearl:
Chromatid separation = Anaphase.

Anatomy-01.question: ৩২) Regarding G2 phase which one is correct?
Anatomy-01.option1: Cells synthesize RNA and protein essential to DNA replication
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is Energy for mitosis is stored. During the G2 phase (Gap 2 phase), the cell prepares for mitosis by synthesizing proteins, accumulating energy, and producing materials required for cell division.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Cells synthesize RNA and protein essential to DNA replication – This occurs mainly during the G1 phase, when the cell prepares for DNA synthesis.

  • Amount of DNA is doubled – DNA replication occurs during the S phase (Synthesis phase), not G2.

  • Longest phase – The G1 phase is generally the longest phase of the cell cycle.

High-yield points:

Cell cycle phases:

  • G1 phase:

    • Cell growth

    • RNA and protein synthesis

    • Preparation for DNA replication

  • S phase:

    • DNA replication → DNA content doubles

  • G2 phase:

    • Protein synthesis for mitosis

    • Energy storage

    • Preparation for cell division

  • M phase:

    • Mitosis and cytokinesis

    • Daughter cells enter G1 phase

Exam pearl:
G2 = Growth preparation for mitosis + energy accumulation.

Anatomy-01.question: ৩৩) The organelles playing an important role in intracellular digestion of the phagocytosed particles are-
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is lysosomes. Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that digest phagocytosed particles after fusion with phagosomes, forming a phagolysosome.

Mechanism:

Phagosome (engulfed particle) + Lysosome → Phagolysosome → Digestion of particle

High-yield points:

  • Lysosome = intracellular digestion organelle

  • Contains:

    • Acid phosphatase

    • Proteases

    • Lipases

    • Nucleases

    • Glycosidases

Other organelles:

  • Ribosome → Protein synthesis

  • Golgi apparatus → Protein modification and packaging

  • Mitochondria → ATP production

Exam pearl:
Phagocytosed particle digestion → Lysosome.

Anatomy-01.question: ৩৪) Which junction helps in the heart’s co-ordinated beats?
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is nexus (gap junction). In cardiac muscle, gap junctions (nexus) allow rapid movement of ions between adjacent cardiac myocytes, enabling electrical conduction and synchronised contraction of the heart.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Tight junction – Prevents passage of substances between cells by forming a seal.

  • Zonula adherens – Provides mechanical attachment between cardiac muscle cells by linking actin filaments.

  • Desmosome – Provides strong mechanical adhesion between cells and prevents separation during contraction.

High-yield points:

Intercellular junctions:

Junction Main function
Gap junction (Nexus) Electrical communication between cells
Desmosome Mechanical strength
Zonula adherens Actin-based adhesion
Tight junction Barrier/sealing

Cardiac intercalated disc contains:

  • Gap junctions → electrical coupling

  • Desmosomes + fascia adherens → mechanical attachment

Exam pearl:
Coordinated cardiac contraction = Gap junction (Nexus).

Anatomy-01.question: ৩৫) Membrane bound organelles-
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is endoplasmic reticulum (ER). The ER is a membrane-bound organelle surrounded by a lipid bilayer and is involved in protein synthesis (rough ER) and lipid synthesis (smooth ER).

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Ribosome – A non-membrane-bound organelle responsible for protein synthesis.

  • Centriole – A non-membrane-bound structure involved in spindle formation during cell division.

  • Microtubule – A component of the cytoskeleton and not membrane-bound.

High-yield points:

Membrane-bound organelles:

  • Nucleus

  • Endoplasmic reticulum

  • Golgi apparatus

  • Mitochondria

  • Lysosomes

  • Peroxisomes

Non-membrane-bound organelles:

  • Ribosomes

  • Centrioles

  • Microtubules

  • Intermediate filaments

Exam pearl:
ER = membrane-bound organelle.

Anatomy-01.question: ৩৬) Mitochondria contains enzymes that take part in following processes except-
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is glycolysis. Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm (cytosol), not inside the mitochondria. Therefore, mitochondria do not contain enzymes for glycolysis.

The other options are correct because they occur in mitochondria:

  • TCA cycle – Occurs in the mitochondrial matrix.

  • Beta oxidation of fatty acid – Occurs mainly in the mitochondrial matrix.

  • Ketogenesis – Occurs in the mitochondrial matrix of liver cells.

High-yield points:

Cellular location of metabolic pathways:

Process Site
Glycolysis Cytoplasm
TCA cycle Mitochondrial matrix
Beta oxidation Mitochondrial matrix
Ketogenesis Mitochondrial matrix (liver)
Electron transport chain Inner mitochondrial membrane

Exam pearl:
Glycolysis = cytosol, not mitochondria.

Anatomy-01.question: ৩৭) Protein synthesis occurs in all of the following except-
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is SER. Smooth endoplasmic reticulum does not participate in protein synthesis; it is mainly involved in lipid synthesis, detoxification, and calcium storage.

The other options are correct because:

  • Ribosome – Site of protein synthesis (translation).

  • RER (Rough endoplasmic reticulum) – Contains ribosomes and synthesizes proteins destined for secretion, membranes, and lysosomes.

  • Mitochondria – Contain their own mitochondrial ribosomes and synthesize some mitochondrial proteins.

High-yield points:

Sites of protein synthesis:

  • Free ribosomes → Cytosolic proteins

  • RER-bound ribosomes → Secretory and membrane proteins

  • Mitochondrial ribosomes → Mitochondrial proteins

SER functions:

  • Lipid synthesis

  • Steroid hormone synthesis

  • Detoxification

  • Ca²⁺ storage (sarcoplasmic reticulum)

Exam pearl:
Protein synthesis → Ribosome/RER; SER → lipid synthesis.

Anatomy-01.question: ৩৮) Brown fat-
Anatomy-01.option1: Fewer in mitochondria than ordinary fat
Anatomy-01.option2: Is found in specific regions of newborn’s body such as-neck
Anatomy-01.option3: Nucleus is situated at the periphery
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is is found in specific regions of newborn’s body such as neck. Brown fat (brown adipose tissue) is abundant in newborns, especially around the neck, interscapular region, kidneys, and large blood vessels. It produces heat through non-shivering thermogenesis.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Fewer in mitochondria than ordinary fat – False. Brown fat contains many mitochondria, which give it its brown colour and allow heat production.

  • Nucleus is situated at the periphery – False. Brown fat cells have a central nucleus.

  • Is unilocular – False. Brown fat is multilocular (contains many small lipid droplets).

High-yield points:

Brown fat vs White fat:

Feature Brown fat White fat
Lipid droplets Multilocular Unilocular
Mitochondria Many Few
Nucleus Central Peripheral
Function Heat production Energy storage
Abundant in Newborns Adults

Exam pearl:
Brown fat = newborn + neck/interscapular region + many mitochondria + thermogenesis.

Anatomy-01.question: ৩৯) Regarding skeletal muscle-
Anatomy-01.option3: Nucleus is single, oval and central
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is striations present. Skeletal muscle fibres show characteristic cross-striations due to the arrangement of actin and myosin filaments into sarcomeres.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Long, cylindrical and branched – Skeletal muscle fibres are long, cylindrical, and unbranched. Branching is a feature of cardiac muscle.

  • Gap junction present – Gap junctions are present in cardiac muscle (intercalated discs), not skeletal muscle.

  • Nucleus is single, oval and central – Skeletal muscle fibres are multinucleated with nuclei located peripherally.

High-yield points:

Skeletal muscle:

  • Long, cylindrical, unbranched fibres

  • Multiple peripheral nuclei

  • Striations present

  • Voluntary muscle

  • No gap junctions

Cardiac muscle:

  • Branched fibres

  • Single central nucleus

  • Intercalated discs with gap junctions

  • Striated

Smooth muscle:

  • No striations

  • Single central spindle-shaped nucleus

Exam pearl:
Skeletal muscle = striated + multinucleated + peripheral nuclei.

Anatomy-01.question: ৪০) Myoepithelial cells are absent in -
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is thyroid gland. Myoepithelial cells are contractile epithelial cells that help in the expulsion of secretions from certain glands. They are absent in the thyroid gland.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Mammary gland – Contains myoepithelial cells around alveoli and ducts to help milk ejection.

  • Sweat gland – Contains myoepithelial cells that assist secretion.

  • Salivary gland – Contains myoepithelial cells around acini and ducts.

High-yield points:

Myoepithelial cells present in:

  • Mammary glands

  • Salivary glands

  • Sweat glands

  • Lacrimal glands

Function:

  • Contractile cells between basement

Anatomy-01.question: ৪১) Which one is the major constituent of plasma membrane?
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is protein. Proteins are the major constituent of the plasma membrane by mass and are responsible for most membrane functions.

Components of plasma membrane:

Protein (~50% by mass) → Transport, receptors, enzymes, cell signalling

Phospholipid (~40%) → Forms the lipid bilayer framework

Cholesterol → Maintains membrane fluidity and stability

Carbohydrate → Cell recognition and glycocalyx formation

The other options are incorrect because:

Phospholipid → Major structural component but not the major constituent by mass.

Cholesterol → Regulates fluidity, but present in smaller amounts.

Carbohydrate → Minor component attached to proteins/lipids.

High-yield cell biology recall:
Major constituent of plasma membrane (by mass) = Protein
Basic structural framework = Phospholipid bilayer

Exam pearl:
Plasma membrane = Lipid bilayer + proteins; proteins are the major functional component.

Anatomy-01.question: ৪২) Primary ossification center is in
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is diaphysis. The primary ossification center appears in the shaft (diaphysis) of a long bone during fetal development. Ossification begins here and later extends toward the ends of the bone.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Epiphysis – Contains the secondary ossification centers, which usually appear after birth.

  • Epiphyseal plate of cartilage – Responsible for lengthwise growth of bone, not the primary ossification center.

  • Metaphysis – The region between diaphysis and epiphysis; contains the growth plate but is not the primary ossification center.

High-yield points:

Long bone ossification:

  • Primary ossification center → Diaphysis (shaft)

  • Secondary ossification centers → Epiphysis (ends)

  • Epiphyseal plate → Longitudinal growth

Exam pearl:
Primary = Diaphysis
Secondary = Epiphysis.

Anatomy-01.question: ৪৩) Which one supports cilia?
৪৪) Packaging center of the cell
৪৫) Type of epithelium in sweat glands
৪৬) Compound alveolar gland is present in
৪৭) Dense irregular connective tissue is present in
৪৮) Major location of Langerhans cell is
৪৯) Cartilaginous joint
৫০) Thickness of cell membrane
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is 5.5 to 10 nm. The plasma membrane thickness is approximately 5–10 nm (commonly quoted around 7.5 nm) and consists of a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins.

The other options are less accurate because:

  • 4.5 to 10 nm – Lower than the commonly accepted range.

  • 6.5 to 10 nm – Within range but not the standard textbook value.

  • 7.5 to 10 nm – Approximate upper range, but the standard answer is usually 5.5–10 nm.

High-yield points:

Plasma membrane:

  • Thickness → 5.5–10 nm

  • Structure → Phospholipid bilayer

  • Model → Fluid mosaic model (Singer and Nicolson, 1972)

Exam pearl:
Cell membrane thickness = ~7.5 nm (range 5.5–10 nm).
